item.title: ‘It’s difficult to be positive’ – Pochettino reacts to Man Utd’s 0-4 defeat
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino has admitted that it is difficult to remain positive after his side suffered a humiliating 4-0 defeat to Brentford in the Premier League on Saturday. Pochettino, who was overseeing his first home match as United manager, expressed disappointment with the result but urged his players to remain united and work together to turn around the club’s fortunes. Speaking after the encounter at Old Trafford, the Argentine said United started the match strongly but struggled after conceding the opening goal. “Difficult to be positive. Very disappointed, disappointed at the same time because I feel sorry for the players,” he said. “The players from the beginning, during 15 to 20 minutes, we were very solid, organisation, structure. I think we were controlling the game. The moment we concede the goal, we should not concede this goal.” Callum Wilson scored twice in the first half to put Brentford in control before Kristoffer Ajer and Kevin Schade added two more goals in the closing stages to complete the visitors’ victory. Pochettino admitted that conceding the first goal affected his players’ confidence and made the contest more difficult for them. He insisted that the squad must remain calm despite the difficult situation, adding that he believes the team will improve with time. “The game goes difficult, the intensity, the nerves. This situation, a situation like this, is affecting your confidence, but we need to be united and stay together and keep pushing. “We are going to push to improve and, of course, it is only a matter of time that we are going to improve. We need to stay together, we need to stay calm. That is why we’re here. We have the responsibility to turn this situation into another way,” he added. Asked whether the challenge at Manchester United had been bigger than he initially anticipated, Pochettino said he knew the club was going through difficult circumstances before accepting the job. The former Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur manager explained that the team’s busy fixture schedule had also made it difficult to implement his ideas, particularly with three matches played within 10 days. “No, we knew it was going to be bigger. That is why we are here. No change in my view. Only that things need time to change in football more. When the fixtures and schedule is so busy,” he said. He added that the players had remained receptive to his instructions and were making efforts to improve despite the disappointing results. “The reaction of the players when we lost 4-0. They tried and they care. That is the most important thing. We need to feel the pain and increase our standards and try to do anything to be much better.” The defeat extended United’s winless run in the Premier League to 10 matches, their longest such streak since going 11 games without a victory between November 1989 and February 1990. item.title: Why I pursued master’s degree while still playing football – Oshoala
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Super Falcons forward Asisat Oshoala has explained that her desire to prepare for life beyond professional football motivated her decision to pursue a Master’s degree in International Sports Management. Oshoala, who recently graduated from the Global Institute of Sport (GIS), said she considered furthering her education important because she intends to remain active in the sporting sector even after her playing career. The six time African Women’s Player of the Year disclosed this in an interview at the Super Falcons’ training camp ahead of their international friendly matches against Algeria. Explaining her decision to return to the classroom, the 32 year old said she wanted to start thinking about her future and other opportunities outside playing football. “I felt like I needed to start thinking about other things, what I want to do in the future, so I needed to study. I own a club and I still want to be in the sporting sector, so it is a good thing to study,” she said. The former Barcelona forward stressed that education would not be a wasted investment, particularly for people who have genuine interests in their chosen fields. She also encouraged professional footballers to make use of the time available to them outside training and matches to develop themselves academically and acquire additional skills. According to her, although footballers dedicate several hours daily to training, they still have enough time to pursue other interests and invest in their personal development. “As a footballer, you know you have like 24 hours in a day, but you have like two or four to six hours to train, so you can use other hours to invest in yourself,” she added. Oshoala’s comments come days after she celebrated her graduation with an MSc in International Sports Management, adding an academic qualification to a football career that has brought her several individual and team honours. Her latest achievement reflects her intention to build a future within the sports industry beyond her exploits on the pitch. The Nigerian international has won the African Women’s Player of the Year award a record six times and lifted four Women’s Africa Cup of Nations titles with the Super Falcons The post Why I pursued master’s degree while still playing football – Oshoala appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: INEC mock polls record large turnouts in Edo, Osun, Nasarawa; ‘We’re satisfied’ – INEC
item.description: *… BVAS worked smoothly in Abuja *We’re satisfied – INEC By Omeiza Ajayi, Ozioruva Aliu, Shina Abubakar & Edwin Philip The residents of Edo, Osun and Nasarawa states turned out massively on Saturday for the mock election exercise conducted by the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, in the designated polling units nationwide. Meanwhile, the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System, BVAS, devices deployed for the nationwide mock presidential election worked smoothly at polling units in Kubwa and Garki. Voters at the Garki unit accredited in less than one minute each. At the City Centre Polling Unit by Area 10, Garki Post Office, in the Abuja Municipal Area Council, AMAC, 18 persons were accredited successfully. Each of them was accredited individually in less than one minute. Three BVAS devices were deployed in the unit. At Polling Unit 024 (PU024), Arab Road/Water Board Junction in Kubwa, Bwari Area Council, the BVAS devices also worked well. Few voters were seen trickling in at intervals. At the Gbazango Garina Hausawa polling unit in Kubwa, INEC officials said they were still waiting for voters hours after opening of poll. There were also a gew voters at Phase 3, by the Model School in Kubwa. Edo State In Benin City, Edo State capital, a visit to Ward 7, Unit 42, New Benin, in Oredo Local Government Area of the state showed an impressive turnout of voters, who came out to participate in the exercise. Speaking with journalists, Mr Daniel Odenigbo, an All Progressives Congress, APC, party agent, described the exercise as peaceful and orderly, commending INEC officials for their efficiency. Odenigbo said the turnout was encouraging, adding that voters were cooperating with the electoral officials to ensure a smooth process. Similarly, a visit to Ward 6 in the same local government area also revealed an encouraging turnout of participants. Speaking with journalists, the APC Ward 6 Chairman in Oredo, Christopher Ize, described the turnout as impressive, expressing optimism that more people would participate as the exercise progressed. Osun Also, in some polling units in Osun State, INEC mock test for the reliability of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System, BVAS, ahead of the 2027 general elections, witnessed good turnout. In most of the polling units visited by Vanguard, the BVAS worked perfectly on facial recognition, while the fingerprints recorded low recognition. The facial recognition takes about 30-40 seconds to recognized voter’s faces after which a dummy ballot is handed to the voter to cast a vote with the process taking about one to two minutes. Polling units visited by Sunday Vanguard in company of the State Resident Electoral Commissioner, REC, included Ward 5, Unit 013, Ajimoko High School, Ilesa West local government, Isokun; Ward 3, Unit 7, Ilesa West local hospital, Igbogi hall; Ward 6, Unit 6, Ilesa West local government, Itaofa junction; Ward 5, Unit 4 and 6, Ilesa East local government, Ijamo; Ward 5, Unit 1, Ede South loc

item.title: ‎Tinubu mourns former Lagos deputy gov, Senator Idiat Adebule
item.description: ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru, Abuja President Bola Tinubu has expressed profound shock and sadness over the sudden passing of former Lagos State Deputy Governor and incumbent Senator representing Lagos West, Senator Idiat Oluranti Adebule. ‎Adebule, 56, died after a brief illness in Lagos. ‎President Tinubu described her death as a painful loss not only to Lagos State and the National Assembly but to the nation as a whole, particularly at a time when her experience, commitment, and contributions to public service are needed. ‎The President recalled the lawmaker’s distinguished record of service and her tenure as Deputy Governor (2015-2019), during which she worked to advance governance and development in the state. ‎He noted the deceased’s political journey, which reflects years of commitment to public administration, education, and empowering citizens, particularly women and the youth. The president lauded her legislative contributions, noting that she continued to demonstrate dedication to democratic governance and the representation of her constituents. President Tinubu extended his heartfelt condolences to her immediate family, the government and people of Lagos State, political associates, members of the All Progressives Congress (APC), the National Assembly, and all those mourning her passing. ‎He prayed that Almighty Allah grant her Aljannatul Firdaus and give her family, friends, and associates the strength to bear this irreparable loss. ‎ ‎ The post ‎Tinubu mourns former Lagos deputy gov, Senator Idiat Adebule appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Netanyahu offers to rotate Israeli premiership with Eisenkot
item.description: Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday proposed a rotating premiership with his main rival Gadi Eisenkot, who would go first, with the latter expected to announce the formation of a new government within days. Proposing a unity government in a social media post, Netanyahu said “my responsibility as a leader requires me to set everything aside… and agree that Gadi Eisenkot will serve first as prime minister, while I will serve as alternate prime minister at the beginning of the term”. The offer came one day after Eisenkot vowed to announce the formation of Israel’s next government by the official deadline of December 6, without using the option of a 14-day extension. He is expected to form a coalition with anti-Netanyahu parties, but his centrist Yashar party has also been conducting negotiations with Netanyahu’s right-wing Likud. On Friday, however, Eisenkot accused Likud of stalling coalition talks in a bid to bring about new elections. “Likud… has been unwilling to compromise and, over two weeks, refused to put a single concrete proposal on the table,” Eisenkot said in a statement. His wide-ranging camp has faced divisions over whether to forge alliances with the ultra-Orthodox parties, the Arab-majority lists, or form a unity government with Likud. Netanyahu opponents scoffed at his offer of a rotating premiership. Youssef Jabareen, leader of the Arab-majority Joint List, which is expected to support an Eisenkot-led government without joining it, wrote: “The democratic majority has decided: this bloodstained, neglectful government must go. It is time to fulfill the shared will of the entire public, Jews and Arabs alike, and remove Netanyahu this (upcoming) week.” “Netanyahu’s proposal is yet another transparent con by a serial fraudster who has deceived every partner and violated every agreement,” wrote former premier Yair Lapid, co-chair of the centrist Beyachad party. Eisenkot’s Yashar party has so far agreed coalition deals with the left-leaning Democrats and the right-wing Israel Beiteinu party. Together, they have a combined total of 36 lawmakers — far short of the 61 needed for a majority in Israel’s 120-seat parliament. Israeli media reported that Mansour Abbas, the leader of the second Arab-Israeli party, Raam, is expected on Saturday to recognise Hamas as a “terror group” — a move that could pave the way for his party to join a possible Eisenkot-led coalition. But some of Eisenkot’s allies have voiced opposition to relying on the support of the Arab-majority lists, which made unprecedented gains in the election. The post Netanyahu offers to rotate Israeli premiership with Eisenkot appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027 Elections: Shettima reduced to Tinubu’s campaign mascot – ADC
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress, ADC, Presidential Campaign Council has accused Vice President Kashim Shettima of abandoning his responsibilities amid Nigerians’ economic hardship to serve as President Bola Tinubu’s campaign attack dog, appearing at political rallies to ridicule former Vice President Atiku Abubakar ahead of the 2027 presidential election. The council said rather than explain what the Tinubu administration had done to ease the rising cost of living, Shettima had chosen to attack the opposition. ADC challenged him to account for the soaring prices of food, transportation and electricity. In a statement by its Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, on Saturday, the council questioned Shettima’s influence in government and accused him of failing to make a meaningful contribution to decisions affecting the lives of ordinary Nigerians. “Vice President Kashim Shettima has reduced his role in this election to that of Tinubu’s campaign mascot: he appears at rallies to mock Atiku Abubakar, but disappears when Nigerians ask why food, transport and electricity have become so expensive,” it said. The campaign council recalled Shettima’s description of former Vice President Yemi Osinbajo as an “ice cream seller” during the 2023 election campaign, challenging him to show what he had achieved nearly four years into the Tinubu administration. “For the holder of Nigeria’s second-highest office, his contribution to the decisions shaping ordinary lives has been remarkably hard to see,” the statement added. It also questioned Shettima’s standing within the administration, alleging that the President’s wife, his son, Seyi Tinubu, the Chief of Staff and FCT Minister, Nyesom Wike, wielded greater influence and commanded more attention than the Vice President. On Shettima’s suggestion that Atiku’s presidential ambition was driven by regional interests, the council insisted that the former Vice President’s campaign had a national appeal, pointing to his running mate, Rotimi Amaechi, who hails from the South. “Atiku has taken his Affordable Life message to voters across Nigeria and his running mate, Rotimi Amaechi, is from the South. Nigerians facing the same hardship across the country do not need Tinubu’s campaign mascot to sort them into regional boxes,” it said. The council also demanded evidence for Shettima’s allegation that Atiku was seeking the presidency to “make money and foment mischief”, describing the accusation as baseless and unbecoming of a holder of the office of Vice President. “Let him produce a shred of evidence or withdraw it. His office does not turn a malicious invention into a fact,” the statement said. On Shettima’s comments about political alliances, the ADC campaign council argued that the APC had also built an alliance to win power, but had failed to translate that political victory into economic relief for Nigerians. “A political handshake is worthless to a parent who cannot afford a m

item.title: Kano deploys forest guards to tackle banditry, kidnapping
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The Kano State Government has deployed newly trained National Forest Guards to tackle banditry, kidnapping, and other security threats, particularly in communities bordering Kaduna and Katsina states. Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf announced this on Saturday during the passing-out parade of the first batch of 1,000 National Forest Guards held at the Kano State Corporate Security Institute, Zakirai, Gabasawa Local Government Area. Yusuf said the initiative was introduced to strengthen security in vulnerable communities and protect forests that could be used as hideouts by criminals. “Insecurity has increasingly become a challenge in some communities across Kano State, particularly those bordering neighbouring states such as Kaduna and Katsina, which have experienced security challenges, including banditry and kidnapping,” Yusuf said. “In our collective efforts to address this menace, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, through the Office of the National Security Adviser, graciously extended this important initiative to Kano State by approving the establishment of the National Forest Guards to complement the existing security architecture,” he added. According to him, the initiative will improve security operations, strengthen intelligence gathering at the grassroots, and protect rural communities. “The establishment and training of the National Forest Guards represent a step towards securing our forests, protecting vulnerable communities, and enhancing intelligence gathering at the grassroots level.” Yusuf urged the graduating guards to work closely with conventional security agencies, gather credible intelligence, and support lawful security operations. He also warned them against abusing their responsibilities. The governor further urged them to uphold discipline, integrity, professionalism, and respect for the rule of law. “You are expected to serve as vigilant guardians of our forests and rural communities. You must work hand in hand with established security agencies, gather credible intelligence, support lawful operations, and contribute positively to maintaining peace and order,” he said. He listed the establishment of the Anti-Phone Snatching Squad, the Kano State Security Neighbourhood Watch Corps, and the Multi-Agency Taskforce on Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking as some of the measures taken by his government to address insecurity. The governor called on residents, traditional rulers, religious leaders, and community groups to cooperate with the Forest Guards, stressing that security was a shared responsibility. “We are committed to supporting security agencies through financial and other forms of assistance,” he added. item.title: Ex-Lagos deputy gov, Senator Adebule, dies at 56
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni Former Lagos State deputy governor and incumbent senator representing Lagos West senatorial district, Dr. Idiat Oluranti Adebule has died barely 24 hours after celebrating her 56th birthday in the state. Adebule, who was seeking re-election for a second term in the Senate, died in the early hours of Saturday. She was pronounced dead by medical experts at a private hospital in Ikeja, G.R.A., Ikeja Local Government Area of the state, where she was admitted after a brief illness. Adebule was said to be battling an undisclosed ailment for several years before she finally succumbed to death on Saturday. She was the deputy to former Governor Akinwunmi Ambode. The Lagos State All Progressives Congress, APC, spokesman, Seye Oladejo, confirmed the death. He described it as “a rude shock.” He prayed the Almighty God forgive her sins and grant her family, friends, and well-wishers the fortitude to bear the irreparable loss. He, however, announced the postponement of the earlier planned Lagos West senatorial campaign rally scheduled for next Monday, November 30. It was learned Senator Adebule was already preparing to attend the campaign rally scheduled for Police College, Ikeja, when the tragedy suddenly occurred. Tinubu mourns Reacting, President Bola Tinubu expressed “profound shock and sadness”. ‎President Tinubu described her death as a painful loss not only to Lagos State and the National Assembly, but to the nation as a whole, particularly at a time when her experience, commitment, and contributions to public service are needed. Tinubu extended his heartfelt condolences to her immediate family, the government and people of Lagos State, political associates, members of the All Progressives Congress (APC), the National Assembly, and all those mourning her passing. Lagos APC Meanwhile, in honour of the late lawmaker, the Director-General of the Lagos State APC PBAT/KOH Campaign Council, Senator Musiliu Obanikoro, has ordered the immediate suspension of all campaign activities across the state until further notice. ​Describing Senator Adebule’s passing as “a painful and irreplaceable loss,” the party noted that halting campaign operations reflects the profound grief within its ranks and the need to accord the late educationist and public servant a dignified farewell. ​”Her years of service, commitment to the progressive ideals of the APC and contributions to the political and developmental advancement of Lagos State will remain indelible,” the statement read. ​The party leadership has also directed all campaign structures, directorates, committees, and supporters to strictly comply with the suspension directive while calling on stakeholders and elected representatives to turn out to pay their final respects on Sunday. ​The Lagos APC also extended its condolences to Senator Adebule’s immediate family, political associates, and the constituents of Lagos West, praying for the peaceful repose of her soul. item.title: Man Utd thrashed 4-0 by Brentford in Pochettino’s home debut
item.description: Manchester United were thrashed 4-0 at home by Brentford on Mauricio Pochettino’s first home match in charge to leave the 20-time English champions still rooted in the Premier League relegation zone. Callum Wilson struck a first-half double before late goals from Kristoffer Ajer and Kevin Schade sealed Brentford’s first win at Old Trafford for 89 years on Saturday. Pochettino replaced the sacked Michael Carrick earlier this month, tasked with turning around the fortunes of a club in steep decline. However, the Argentine could barely have imagined a worst start after also losing 4-0 away to Liverpool in his first match in charge last weekend. For the first time in 65 years, United have conceded four goals in three consecutive league matches. That shocking defensive record has plunged the Red Devils into a battle for survival. Only Crystal Palace sit below United and Pochettino’s men could slip to the foot of the table if the Eagles beat Hull on Sunday. Pochettino came out fighting after a series of refereeing decisions went against his side against Liverpool and in a controversial 2-2 draw at Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League on Wednesday. But there was no hiding place for the new boss or his players after their latest embarrassment. Brentford were missing first-choice striker Igor Thiago through suspension, but it mattered little as his deputy Wilson took advantage of United’s disorganised defence. An encouraging start by the home side was quickly forgotten when Wilson lashed home a brilliant finish to open the scoring on 19 minutes. The former Newcastle and West Ham striker then doubled his tally from Dango Ouattara’s pass 13 minutes later. The end of Carrick’s reign was marked by brief flickers of United resistance in comebacks to beat Roma and salvage a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa. Youri Tielemans smashed against the crossbar as United pressed for a route back into the game in the second half. But their inability to defend ended any hope of a fightback as Ajer was given way too much space to fire in from a corner. Schade then completed the rout in stoppage time as Brentford climbed to fifth and within one point of the top four. item.title: Low turnout mars INEC mock polls in Bauchi
item.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) on Saturday recorded low turnout of voters during its mock accreditation exercise conducted in selected polling units in Bauchi Local Government Area of Bauchi State ahead of the 2027 general elections. The exercise, aimed at testing the functionality of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System, BVAS, ahead of the elections, witnessed poor participation in some polling units visited by Vanguard. At Bakari Dukur Primary School polling unit, Vanguard observed that only a handful of voters were present, with fewer than five people seen waiting to undergo the accreditation process as INEC officials prepared for the exercise. A similar situation was observed at Yelwa Maternity Ward polling unit, where only a few voters turned out to participate in the exercise. Vanguard also observed that some voters encountered difficulties with the BVAS machines during the capturing of their information, while others arrived late, attributing their delay to the sanitation exercise observed by the state. However, the situation was slightly different at Makama/Sarki Baki polling units, where turnout was relatively fair, although some voters also arrived late. An INEC official at the polling unit attributed the late arrival of voters to the sanitation exercise, which affected their movement to the polling centres. An APC agent and observer at Makama, Yakubu Abduhamid, said poor awareness about the mock accreditation exercise contributed to the low turnout, noting that many residents appeared uninterested in the exercise. He, however, said those who participated at Sarki Baki polling unit conducted themselves peacefully, despite what he described as an unimpressive turnout. As of the time of filing this report, Vanguard had visited more than two polling units in Bauchi metropolis and observed that the exercise commenced late in some locations, while participation remained low. Some voters blamed the situation on inadequate awareness and the sanitation exercise, which they said hindered their timely arrival at the polling units. The post Low turnout mars INEC mock polls in Bauchi appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027; Yilwatda hands APC flags, brooms to Mbah, Nwifuru, Opah
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja National Chairman of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), Professor Nentawe Yilwatda, has presented the party’s flags and its symbolic broom to its governorship candidates in Enugu, Abia and Ebonyi states and told them to turn their campaigns into landslide victories in the 2027 general elections. The candidates are Peter Ndubuisi Mbah of Enugu State, Eric Chinemuecheya Opah of Abia State and Francis Ogbonna Nwifuru of Ebonyi State. In a statement by his Special Adviser on Media and Information Strategy, Abimbola Tooki, Yilwatda told the candidates to fly the party’s flag proudly in their states, carry its message to every community and constituency, and mobilise voters for resounding wins at the polls. The presentation took place on Friday at the APC presidential campaign rally in Enugu, led by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. Yilwatda made it through to Vice President Kashim Shettima in the presence of governors, members of the National Working Committee (NWC), elected officials and party stakeholders from across the country. He described the exercise as a demonstration of the party’s confidence in its candidates and its resolve to consolidate its strength across the federation. Yilwatda reserved his most emphatic charge for Nwifuru, the Ebonyi State Governor and APC governorship candidate, whom he urged to fly the party’s flag high and ensure that Ebonyi delivers an overwhelming harvest of votes for the APC. He told Opah, the party’s Abia governorship candidate, to take the flag across the state, deepen the party’s appeal at the grassroots and mobilise voters to deliver victory in the 2027 governorship election. Using the broom as an electoral metaphor, the National Chairman urged the candidates to make the most of every political opportunity to sweep votes for the APC on election day. He said the broom stands for more than the party’s identity. In his words as reported in the statement, it carries the party’s enduring message of unity, collective strength, political organisation and the determination to win through coordinated efforts. Yilwatda called on party leaders, members, supporters and grassroots mobilisers in the three states to close ranks and work together for the success of the candidates and the party’s wider electoral aspirations. He said the burden of winning elections does not rest on the candidates alone. Every party member, he said, has a role in strengthening the party’s structures, widening its support base and communicating the achievements and vision of the Tinubu administration. The National Chairman also pointed to President Tinubu’s leadership and the collective commitment of party stakeholders to consolidating the APC’s political dominance and delivering on its Renewed Hope Agenda. The Enugu rally, he said, gave the party another opportunity to show its organisational capacity, national reach and determination to approach the 2027 elections as a united political family. item.title: 2027 : Atiku, Obi relying on regional support to win election, Shettima says
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Vice President Kashim Shettima has accused former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi of relying on regional support in their bid to win the 2027 presidential election. Shettima made the remarks on Saturday during the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign rally in Enugu, where he questioned the opposition candidates’ campaign strategies and their efforts to build support across the country. He said Obi had visited 17 states, including all five states in the South-East and all South-South states except Rivers, but had made limited visits to other regions. According to Shettima, Obi had visited only Kaduna State in the North and Lagos State in the South-West. He also accused the Labour Party’s 2023 presidential candidate of attempting to use religious divisions to advance his political ambition, insisting that elections could not be won through division. “You cannot win election through divisions. We win elections through negotiation, through compromises, through bridge building,” the Vice-President said. Shettima also criticised Atiku’s campaign activities, claiming that the former vice-president had visited only six states and had not travelled to any state in Southern Nigeria. “My brother Atiku Abubakar, he has so far visited six states in the Federation. He has not visited one state in Southern Nigeria. He has concentrated purely in the North,” he said. The Vice-President argued that presidential candidates needed support beyond their traditional political strongholds to secure victory, citing former President Muhammadu Buhari’s eventual success after building an alliance with the South-West. He said Buhari’s support in the North alone had not been enough to secure the presidency until he formed an alliance with the South-West. Shettima expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu would defeat the opposition candidates in the 2027 election. item.title: Poor turnout, smooth BVAS operation mark INEC mock polls in Kebbi
item.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) mock accreditation and voting exercise in selected polling units in Kebbi State on Saturday recorded low voter turnout, although the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) machines operated without reported malfunctions. The exercise witnessed a predominantly female turnout, with relatively few male voters seen at several polling units visited. At Aliero Housing Estate 006 Primary School polling unit, female voters turned out for accreditation, while only a few male voters were sighted. Security personnel, including officers of the Police, Department of State Services (DSS), Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) and State Security Service (SCIB), were deployed to provide security during the exercise. INEC ad hoc staff at the polling unit confirmed that the BVAS machines were functioning effectively during voter authentication. A visit to Gwadangaji 001 polling unit also showed a low turnout, with a few female voters presenting themselves for accreditation and no male voters sighted at the time. The voters were seen checking their names on the lists displayed on the walls before proceeding with the exercise. However, at Justice Ibrahim Umar polling unit in the GRA NEPA area, a relatively large number of female voters turned out for the mock exercise. The ad hoc staff confirmed that the two BVAS machines provided for the polling unit were working effectively, adding that no malfunction had been recorded since the exercise commenced at 9 a.m. Meanwhile, an APC stakeholder, Alhaji Abubakar ABK, described the exercise as impressive and peaceful. He attributed the participation of female voters to what he described as the humanitarian interventions of Governor Idris, expressing optimism that voters would turn out in large numbers during the January 2027 general elections. ABK urged voters to maintain the peaceful conduct witnessed during the mock exercise when participating in the main elections in 2027. The post Poor turnout, smooth BVAS operation mark INEC mock polls in Kebbi appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, organised mocked polls across the country today with mixed results and turnouts. The exercise was to test INEC’s preparedness for the 2027 elections, expecially the technical aspects. However, despite reports of poor numbers, the INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, expressed satisfaction with the conduct of the nationwide mock accreditation exercise. He assured Nigerians of the commission’s readiness to deliver credible elections in 2027. Amupitan, who visited Jos on Saturday to monitor the exercise, inspected polling locations, including Obasanjo Model School in Jos South Local Government Area, where he observed voter accreditation and the performance of electoral technology. Speaking to journalists, the INEC chairman described the turnout and conduct of the exercise as impressive. “You can see yourself that it is very impressive. The turnout is very good,” he said. Uploaded results Meanwhile, about 1,995 results (approximately 12%) of the 17,614 expected, had been uploaded as of 3:09 pm on Saturday in the nationwide INEC mock presidential election. The Mock Accreditation and Result Upload Exercise, which started at 8:30a.m., ended at 2:30pm. However, more than 30 minutes later, the portal puts the “Percentage uploaded” at 11.33 per cent. Its last recorded upload came at 3:09:11 pm from polling unit 32/04/05/005, at press time. Low turnout in Lagos Low turnout of eligible voters marred the mock accreditation exercise conducted in parts of Lagos State, with some voters blaming the commission’s inadequate publicity. Polling agents expressed concern over the poor participation when Vanguard visited some of the designated polling units in Ijegun, Satellite Town and Festac, in the Amuwo-Odofin area of the state. An INEC polling agent at one of the polling units said only about 40 of the 250 registered voters had participated in the exercise as of the time of the visit. …in Katsina, too; poor publicity Also, low voter turnout and inadequate public awareness characterised the mock accreditation exercise conducted by lNEC in Katsina State on Saturday, ahead of the 2027 general elections. Vanguard monitoring of the exercise at Star Election Polling Unit, Wakilin Kudu 1, Kofar Gidan Iro Isansi, Rafin Dadi, showed that only a few voters turned out to participate, although some were successfully accredited. The low participation raised concerns about the level of public sensitisation and awareness among eligible voters regarding the importance of the exercise. Apathy in Abia In Abia Stste, voter apathy marred the mock accreditation and result-upload exercise conducted by INEC, with several polling units recording zero or minimal turnout. item.title: 2027: Vote out APC, Adebayo urges Nigerians
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Presidential candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), Prince Adewole Adebayo, has urged Nigerians to vote out the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) in the 2027 general election, saying the country’s future should be determined by its citizens rather than a privileged political group. Adebayo also called on Nigerians to move beyond complaints about bad governance and participate actively in the electoral process, insisting that voting remained the most effective democratic instrument for changing an administration. He spoke during an SDP town hall meeting with party leaders, candidates and supporters in Nasarawa State, where he criticised the APC over the economic and security challenges confronting the country. He said: “A bad government does not go by you abusing it. A bad government does not go by you shouting. A government goes by you voting it out. The government does not care whether you abuse it, but it cares whether you vote. So, you must vote.” The SDP candidate said the central question before Nigerians in 2027 was whether the country belonged to its citizens or a privileged group exercising political and economic influence. “What is at stake in 2027 is whether Nigeria belongs to the people or whether Nigeria belongs to the cabal. You must say with your mouth and tell your neighbours that Nigeria belongs to the Nigerian people,” he said. Adebayo said the SDP was offering Nigerians an alternative political and economic programme focused on tackling poverty, insecurity, unemployment and the rising cost of living. He said the party’s manifesto contained proposals aimed at improving citizens’ welfare and ensuring that public resources were directed towards addressing their most pressing needs. On the economy, he promised that an SDP administration would reduce the pump price of petrol to N200 per litre without fuel subsidy, arguing that this would be achievable through measures to eliminate corruption and improve efficiency in the petroleum sector. “We will give you petrol for N200 per litre without subsidy. We will sell it for N200, and NNPC will still make a profit because we will stop funding corruption,” he said. Addressing food security, Adebayo described Nasarawa and neighbouring states as strategically positioned to contribute significantly to national food production, citing their agricultural potential. “Nasarawa alone can feed Nigeria. Nasarawa, Plateau, Kogi, Kaduna and the Federal Capital Territory have the capacity to feed the whole of Africa,” he said. He promised that an SDP government would implement policies to make food affordable and ensure Nigerians had access to basic necessities. On education, the presidential candidate pledged free, compulsory and qualitative education, particularly for children currently excluded from formal schooling. item.description: Kodak’s retro Charmera comes in multiple colors and styles. | Photos: Andrew Liszewski / The Verge We wouldn’t normally recommend a bad camera, but we’ll make an exception for the Kodak Charmera . As my colleague Andrew Liszewski pointed out in his review , the tiny retro keychain camera takes pretty lackluster photos, yet it’s charming enough that he kept using it anyway. That makes it a great gift for anyone who loves cute gadgets, especially now that it’s on sale at Amazon and B&H Photo for an all-time low of $29.74 (about $5 off). Kodak Charmera Keychain Digital Camera Where to Buy: $34.99 $29.74 at Amazon $34.99 $29.74 at B&H Photo The Charmera is small enough to carry on your keys and comes in a blind box, so you won’t know which of the six retro designs or the rarer transparent version you’re getting until you open it. It’s a simple point-and-shoot with a tiny LCD screen, and its 1,440×1,080-pixel photos often look fuzzy and washed out. Some of the built-in effects can make the results more interesting, though. Liszewski had some fun with the black-and-white mode and found that the red, blue, yellow, and gray pixel filters could produce bolder two-tone images. Video and audio quality are poor, too, and you can’t adjust much to improve them. Still, for a $30 keychain, it offers a surprising amount to play with. The Charmera isn’t something you’d want to rely on for an important occasion, but it can be fun to experiment with. Liszewski found that even though most pictures weren’t worth keeping, he’d occasionally get one interesting enough to share. That makes it a fun stocking stuffer for someone who loves cute, unusual gadgets. Read our full Kodak Charmera impressions .

How moon dust and recycled cardboard could help NASA build its lunar base
item.description:
Julian Dossett is a freelance writer living in Santa Fe, New Mexico. He primarily covers the rocket industry and space exploration and, in addition to science writing, contributes travel stories to New Mexico Magazine. In 2022 and 2024, his travel writing earned IRMA Awards. Previously, he worked as a staff writer at CNET. He graduated from Texas State University in San Marcos in 2011 with a B.A. in philosophy. He owns a large collection of sci-fi pulp magazines from the 1960s.

The high cost of building on the moon has led to wide-ranging research on how to make use of the moon's most plentiful resource: the dusty regolith that covers its surface. Right now, lunar shipping runs about $544,000 per pound ($1.2 million per kilogram), so anything that astronauts can make on the moon using existing materials could help a lot. Scientists have already proposed using regolith for building 3D-printed bricks , solar arrays , and even as soil to grow potatoes . Now, a team of researchers from Purdue University in Indiana have developed an aerogel made from simulated regolith for insulating lunar habitats. New aerogels created by Purdue University researchers, made of cellulose and lunar regolith simulant, could pave the way for insulating materials made on the moon. (Image credit: Purdue University photo/John Underwood) "Sustaining a long-term presence on the moon will require us to rethink how we use local resources," Wei, professor in Purdue's James Tarpo Jr. and Margaret Tarpo Department of Chemistry, said in a Nov. 19 statement . NASA has said that it wants a long-term, sustainable moon base up and running by 2032, a goal it aims to achieve via its Artemis program . "Rather than relying on Earth to supply everything we need, we're exploring how materials already available on the moon, including waste generated by its inhabitants, could be upcycled into something essential for safe and livable habitats," Wei said. The aerogel that the Purdue researchers have been working on is a mix of fiber from cardboard waste, called cellulose, and a material that simulates regolith. They said that it could protect the people living in habitats from the moon's drastic temperature swings. "Imagine an aerogel as a high-tech thermos for a lunar base," Jacob Staker, a graduate researcher working on the study, said in the same statement. "Most of it consists of empty space that insulates the interior, helping it maintain the temperature of what's inside." The idea here is not to create the best aerogel possible, Wei said, but that "we're looking for the sweet spot where we can get the properties we need with the limited resources we have available" on the moon. The research was published in September in the journal ACS Sustainable Chemistry & Engineering.

item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 28, 1967: Astronomers Jocelyn Bell and Antony Hewish disover the 1st pulsar with Little Green Men 1 signal
item.description: null On November 28, 1967, astronomers found the first pulsar. A pulsar is a super-dense star that rotates super fast. As the pulsar spins, it emits two beams of light in opposite directions. When astronomers look at a pulsar, it looks like a star that's flickering on and off at a steady, constant pace. The first pulsar was observed by Jocelyn Bell Burnell and Antony Hewish. They were looking at the constellation Vulpecula when they saw a star flickering with regular pulses separated by 1.33 seconds. At first they had no idea what it was, so they jokingly nicknamed the signal Little Green Men 1. After more pulsars were discovered, they were able to rule out aliens. This chart tracked the signal of the first pulsar ever discoverered on Nov. 28, 1967. (Image credit: Cambridge University Library/Wikipedia) Why it mattered Pulsars are naturally occurring phenomena, and they can be handy tools for astronomers . For example, some pulsars are extremely accurate clocks. Because pulsars rotate, their emission of beams of radiation is observed at regular intervals. Until Burnell's discovery, astronomers did not know if neutron stars existed, let alone if they could be observed. "Suddenly, it turned out that nature has provided an incredibly precise way to observe these objects, something that has led to many later advances," said Edward Witten, chairman of the selection committee for the Fundamental Physics Breakthrough Prize, which in 2018 was awarded to Burnell . Among other applications, the observation of pulsars are one of the best ways astronomers have for testing Albert Einstein's theory of general relativity. The spinning stars have also been used as a navigation tool for spacecraft moving out beyond low Earth orbit. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.description: A voter at polling unit 001 in Barnawa, Kaduna South Local Government Area, captured attention on Saturday, as she made different frustrating facial expressions while being captured on the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) during the INEC’s mock accreditation exercise in Kaduna State. Our correspondent, who monitored the exercise, noted that a voter spent more than five minutes completing the accreditation and voting process due to network challenges affecting the machine. The exercise is expected to simulate the Presidential election, with polling units opening by 8:30 a.m. and accreditation running from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. Meanwhile, one of the voters at polling unit 002, Narayi Primary School, in Kaduna State, Rebecca Oladipo, has expressed frustration over the absence of the Independent National Electoral Commission’s officials at the mock accreditation on Saturday. Oladipo, who said she arrived at the polling unit for the INEC mock accreditation exercise at 10:30 am, questioned the commission’s preparedness to conduct a credible election in 2027, expressing concern that the mock election, which is expected to test INEC’s operational readiness, appears to be starting on a shaky note. According to her, the delay left those who turned up for the exercise waiting without knowing when the exercise would commence. Rebecca Oladipo “I’m here at Narayi Primary School, one of the wards chosen for the mock exercise. I have been here for the past two hours. INEC is supposed to start the exercise at 8:30. Now we are at around 10:30, and we are yet to see them. “This is really disheartening because a lot of people have been here. Security agencies have been here; even I came to meet them here. One or two voters have been here, and they left. “I’m using this opportunity to say to INEC that we in Narayi ward are not happy because we heard that other wards have started the exercises, so we should not be left behind. “I’m using this opportunity to tell INEC that in the main election, please, please, let it not be like this. It has always been like this in the previous elections. Maybe because Narayi people are good and kind people. They are quiet people. “But please, I hope that everyone knows that the 2027 general election is a critical one. So, we are begging that they should make everything available. “Whatever may make them come late during the 2027 election, they should please avoid it.” The mock exercise, expected to simulate the Presidential election, is expected to open by 8:30 a.m., and accreditation will run from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. The post [PHOTOS] Moment Voter Makes Frustrating Facial Expressions While Being Captured On INEC’s BVAS appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Space in Macy’s 100 Thanksgiving Day parades
item.description: null The 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade is sure to be a blast, but it is a bit light on "space." According to previews provided by the department store chain, the founder of the New York City holiday celebration, space fans turning up or tuning in to catch sight of an astronaut or other nod to NASA will have only a returning rocket to look forward to on Saturday (Nov. 28). (The parade has been postponed two days from Thursday, Nov. 26, due to bad weather.) Not that Macy's (or the space agency) has hinted about anything cosmic planned for the 100th parade; it's only that the event has had a long history of celebrating space exploration with its floats and balloons. "For our 100th parade, we're creating a celebration of unprecedented scale and will deliver an unforgettable Thanksgiving for millions across the country," said Sharon Otterman, Macy's chief marketing officer, in a statement . First held in 1924 for Macy's colleagues, their friends and families, the Thanksgiving Day Parade has been held every year with the exception of a three-year break during World War II. Spanning longer than the dawn of the Space Age, the space race and NASA's entire 68-year history, the celebration has integrated space themes into its displays, even before the first rocket flew beyond Earth's atmosphere . Weighty weightless man The earliest space-themed feature of the parade may have been the "Space Ship," a float that made its first appearance in the 19th procession in 1945 and in various configurations — with and without astronauts and planets — appeared on and off through 1962. Perhaps more memorable, though, and certainly much larger, was the "Spaceman" (or, more appropriately, "The Giant Spaceman"). The 70-foot-long (21-meter) helium balloon made its debut in 1952, nine years before the Soviet Union's Yuri Gagarin became the first person in space. Described by Macy's as an "artist's conception of a visitor from another planet," the humanoid figure had a black spacesuit , a silver helmet and boots, a jet propulsion backpack and a black rocket gun. Once the heaviest balloon in the parade, the "Spaceman" was created by the Goodyear Tire and Rubber Company years before anyone had entered space. (Image credit: Macy's) Ironically, for a figure garbed for the weightless environment of space, the Spaceman was for a long time the parade's heaviest giant balloon. At 600 pounds (272 kilograms), it was only tied by the Pink Panther in 1988 and then exceeded two years later by Bart Simpson. The rubber Spaceman was created by Goodyear Tire, the same company that contributed hardware to NASA's Apollo program , including the wire mesh non-pneumatic tires for the lunar roving vehicle. The Spaceman survived being torn when it was caught with a lamppost in 1955, and a helium shortage resulting in it and other balloons being filled with air and held up by cranes in 1958. It was retired after its seventh appearance in 1959, and ultimately was destroyed. 'The First Men on the

item.title: PHOTOS: Low Turnout as INEC begins Mock Election
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) commenced its mock elections in Borno State to test-run voting equipment and logistical readiness ahead of the 2027 general elections. However, the exercise recorded a low voter turnout in some polling units visited by our correspondent due to what many residents described as “a lack of awareness”. The exercise, designed to evaluate the deployment of election personnel and the functionality of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) across all 27 local government areas of the state, also faced a slow start in some polling units. Across Jere and Maiduguri Metropolitan Councils security personnel, including police officers and the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) and Road Safety Officials, were present early at some polling units, INEC officials arrived late. Yul recalls Pete Edochie’s final moments 3 killed, many injured as rival youth groups clash in Cross River At the Bulama Jidda polling unit in Gomari Airport, voting commenced at 8:44 a.m. after officials arrived, slightly behind schedule. However, poll workers and voters at the station confirmed that the BVAS machines functioned efficiently. “There is actually a low turnout, but the use of BVAS is smooth. At some point, we are using it offline, but will upload it when we reach areas with a robust network,” one polling unit officer stated. Interviews with residents across various areas revealed that public awareness of the exercise was generally poor, with many locals unaware that the mock election was taking place. At the Gwange III polling unit, turnout was similarly low. Some prospective voters said they encountered some technical hitches during accreditation, reporting that the BVAS failed to capture their fingerprints and facial features. Speaking on condition of anonymity, an Ad-hoc staff, noted that affected individuals were not issued ballot papers. Instead, their details were compiled for INEC to review and resolve prior to the general elections. At the Government House polling unit (Unit 001, Maisandari Ward), where voter turnout was notably impressive, the process ran without hitches. Abacha Anas, the Electoral Officer for Operations for INEC in the Maiduguri Metropolitan Council, described the exercise as smooth and successful.

item.title: 2026 Kindle Paperwhite review: Page-turn buttons are back, for a price
item.description: Supply pressures, shortages, and inflation have pushed tech prices relentlessly upward over the last half-decade, and even basic gadgets haven't been immune. That's why you can spend $385 on a Raspberry Pi, or why the cheapest Amazon Kindle in 2026 costs more than the midrange one from a few years ago . "New thing, better features, same price" used to be a reliable formula, but now you're lucky if you can get the same thing for barely more than before. The 2024 Kindles all came with small price increases, but the 2026 models make them look like stellar deals. The $160 Kindle Paperwhite from two years ago wipes the floor with this year's $150 Kindle in just about every conceivable way, from screen size to front light quality to waterproofing—something to consider if you're choosing between a used or refurbished Paperwhite and one of these new models. The flagship of the now five-model-large monochrome Kindle family is the $250 2026 Paperwhite Signature Edition, which takes the core specs of the new $200 Paperwhite and puts it in a sturdy iPad-esque aluminum case instead of the typical plastic. item.title: 12 grains of dust found high in Earth's atmosphere reveal secrets of water at the edge of the solar system
item.description: A dozen grains of dust that have wandered in from the distant Kuiper Belt beyond Neptune were found floating in Earth's stratosphere. And it turns out they hold the secrets of a special kind of 'heavy' water that seems to be surprisingly abundant in the outer solar system. When analyzed by a team of scientists the 12 dust grains, which were captured by NASA's stratospheric ER-2 research aircraft, show signs of having interacted with a form of water that contains heavy oxygen isotopes. This is important because to better understand how the planets formed, scientists are seeking to understand how various materials were distributed around the early solar system 4.5 billion years ago. If there is a reservoir of heavy water out in the solar system's hinterlands, understanding how that water got out there and stayed out there will inform models that describe the growth of the planets. Water consists of two hydrogen atoms and an oxygen atom. What we usually refer to as heavy water is water that contains a heavy isotope of hydrogen. An isotope is an atom that contains the usual number of protons for that element, but a different number of neutrons . Elements are determined by the number of protons they contain. For example, hydrogen always has just one proton. Ordinary 'light' hydrogen has 1 proton and no neutrons, but its heavy isotopes – deuterium and tritium – contain 1 and 2 neutrons, respectively, in addition to the proton. However, there's another kind of water that features heavy isotopes of oxygen instead. Ordinary 'light' oxygen is made from 8 protons and 8 neutrons and is hence known as oxygen-16 but some oxygen isotopes can have 9 or 10 neutrons, and we call these isotopes oxygen-17 or -18. There have been a few clues that such a reservoir exists. Mineralogical evidence from a single carbonaceous chondritic meteorite and measurements from comet 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko indicated the presence of minerals that had formed from interactions between silicate rock and abundant oxygen-heavy variety of water, but it was not clear whether these were isolated instances or a clue to something more widespread. An illustration comparing the locations of the solar system planets to the Kuiper Belt and the Oort Cloud, a theorized shell of icy objects at the farthest reaches of our solar system. (Image credit: ESA) Another data point comes from NASA's Genesis mission, which launched in 2001 and collected particles from the solar wind that were subsequently returned to Earth for study. The analysis of these particles indicated that the sun contains proportionally more ordinary 'light' oxygen than Earth and most meteorites. This suggests that there could be an outwards gradient of increasing abundance of heavy oxygen. Yet the Kuiper Belt is so far away that it makes finding more evidence for this difficult. However, rather than having to go to the Kuiper Belt to sample the water-ice there, dust grains can bring a little bit of the Kuiper Belt to us. T

item.title: Quantum: 'Five years, that's all we got…'
item.description: SC26 in Chicago had the usual quantum booths, discussions, and hallway optimism. A lot of people were talking about integration with classical HPC and Slurm scheduling for quantum processors, co-design platforms, and GPU-accelerated error correction tools. That part is real and useful. What was harder to find was any result that changed the basic math on when quantum systems will actually do something a supercomputer can't already handle better. I had a long conversation in St. Louis (SC25) with a contact who works deep in quantum and has spent decades in HPC. He's not a skeptic for sport, although that can be fun, sure. Over a grifted free dinner in Chicago (the best kind), his take this year remains the same: the hype keeps outrunning the error rates. Quantum computers generate too many errors to give usable answers on anything interesting. Fixing that is the whole game. And that's a five-year game, minimum. Much like the Bowie anthem in the title. Qubits by the numbers There are two kinds of qubits. Physical qubits are the actual hardware: ions, superconducting circuits, and atoms in a trap. Logical qubits are the ones that do the computation. Each logical qubit is built out of many physical ones so the system can detect and correct errors while it runs. With the traditional surface-code approach, one logical qubit often needs somewhere between 500 and 2,000 physical qubits backing it up, depending on the hardware and the code. One logical qubit by itself is useless. Estimates for basic scientific modeling and small-scale simulation sit in the 100-to-500 logical-qubit range. Take the midpoint of 300. At the low end of the overhead that is 150,000 physical qubits. At the high end it is several million. That is only for early science. Commercial work like molecular mapping for pharma, large optimization problems, complex financial models, pushes into the thousands of logical qubits. National-security and encryption-related work sits even higher. Those numbers have not magically shrunk. A system that can map a modestly sized drug molecule, or run a materials simulation that is still too slow on classical machines, is the kind of workload people actually mean when they talk about useful quantum advantage. Until the logical-qubit counts get there with error rates low enough to finish the job, those problems stay on the machines we already know how to build. Ok, so let's just scale it up This is the world of HPC, we know how to scale stuff, right? Yes, but this isn't a matter of adding a few more racks. Scaling to an additional few hundred thousand physical qubits is not a rack or two or ten. It's probably a dedicated building with its own cryogenics, control electronics, and power draw that is still measured in megawatts even before you get useful logical capacity. This is why cutting the massive gap between logical and physical qubits is critical if quantum is going to become even narrowly useful. Signs of (incremental) improvement There is a newe

item.title: Unkernel and Trynix just transported computing to 2035
item.description: What's the difference between just-for-fun demo hacks, and serious carefully designed large-scale software architecture? It's the quick-and-dirty jobs that end up transforming computing. A blog post earlier this week called 2035 came early led the Reg FOSS desk down what we thought was a fascinating, and possibly quite scary, rabbit-hole… but it turned out to be an entire warren. We thought we were still in 2026, but in turns out that in some ways, tech just leaped forward a decade. To try to convey the point of this blog post – why what had been just a fun clever little hack has the potential to take half a century of OS and hypervisor design and throw it out of the nearest window – will take quite a lot of unpacking. If you bear with us, we will try to walk you through it. To get started, we need to go back a decade or more. Stick with this: there are laughs, as well as hammers taken to beloved ideas. The year of 2035 and the ideas around that come from a remarkable talk by Gary Bernhardt of Destroy All Software, which is both funny and highly educational. It will really massively assist understanding what this article and the technology is all about if you have the time to watch the talks. The Reg FOSS desk is not at all fond of spoken-word video as a medium – we much prefer to read than listen – but the three talks we're going to mention are golden, among the very best presentations this century in all of computing and IT. Seriously, they are worth your time. As a preface, before we go into Bernhardt's half-hour information-dense talk, let's warm up with a four-minute funny one. But first, let's look at the context for that. Step 0: JavaScript is the language of web programming In 2009, Jeff Atwood laid this out in an article called All Programming is Web Programming . It's still coming true today. Software is getting very blurred around the edges. The entire SaaS industry means that massive organizations run on web apps. Tech like Electron embeds a web browser inside JavaScript apps built in Node.js, while Progressive Web Apps make websites look like local program windows. The most popular desktop Linux in the world is ChromeOS Flex, which doesn't support local native applications at all. Everything is browser windows, even the desktop. It's all built in JavaScript. And yet… Step 1: JavaScript is kind of weird and kind of bad. Bernhardt made this case in 2012, with a celebrated lightning talk called Wat , from the CodeMash conference in 2012. Wat walks through a whole list of examples of how JavaScript is a very strange programming language and does very strange things that are not at all what you might expect. Some of the jokes will make more sense to programmers, but we reckon anyone who has ever fought with a recalcitrant bit of software will get some laughs from it – and that probably applies to all readers of The Register. Step 2: JavaScript is in the process of conquering the world. Bernhardt moved on to much bigger ideas at PyCon 2014

item.title: APOD: 2026 November 28 – Apollo 17 VIP Site Anaglyph
item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 28 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Apollo 17 VIP Site Anaglyph Explanation: Get out your red/blue glasses and check out this stereo scene from Taurus-Littrow valley on the Moon! The color anaglyph features a detailed 3D view of Apollo 17’s Lunar Rover in the foreground. Behind it lies the Lunar Module and distant lunar hills. Because the world was going to be able to watch the Lunar Module’s ascent stage liftoff via the rover’s TV camera, this parking place was also known as the VIP Site. In December of 1972 , Apollo 17 astronauts Eugene Cernan and Harrison Schmitt spent about 75 hours on the Moon, while colleague Ronald Evans orbited overhead . The crew returned with 110 kilograms of rock and soil samples, more than from any of the other lunar landing sites. Cernan and Schmitt are still the last to walk ( or drive ) on the Moon . Tomorrow’s picture: dark cloud Date: November 28, 2026 Credit: Gene Cernan , Apollo 17 , NASA ; Anaglyph by Erik van Meijgaarden Authors & editors: Jerry Bonnell, Cecilia Chirenti, Robert Nemiroff, Keighley Rockcliffe A service of: ASD at NASA / GSFC , NASA Science Activation & Michigan Tech. item.description: Zlatan, Peruzzi, and Shoday from the official visuals for their collaborative single “Inferno.” Photo Credit: Peruzzi/Instagram Between Friday traffic in Lagos, Sunday afternoon wind-downs, and the official countdown to Detty December already kicking into gear across Nigeria, the final weekend of November arrives with a stacked line-up of fresh visuals worth queuing up on your screen. From street-hop swagger and a ninth-anniversary gospel love note by one of Nollywood and Afrobeats’ favourite couples to a pan-African dancefloor link-up between Benin and Tanzania, these five music videos deliver plenty to replay all weekend long. Skilful – Asake Lifted from his chart-topping 2026 album M$NEY, Asake brings his unmistakable log-drum bounce and choir-backed street-hop cadence to the official visual for “Skilful”. Built around his nimble Yoruba wordplay and self-assured reflections on hard-earned success, the record moves at an upbeat, club-ready tempo made for late-night drives and weekend speakers. On screen, Mr. Money leans straight into high-fashion street theatrics, pairing bold styling with fast-paced choreography and tight framing that keeps your eyes locked on every beat drop. “On My Way” – Susu x Banky W. You may have noticed Adesua Etomi-Wellington—performing here as Susu—kept an unusually low profile for much of 2026, and the backstory behind her new duet with Banky W. puts every lyric into focus. Behind the scenes, she spent months navigating back-to-back hospital visits, scans, tests, and medical procedures across Nigeria and the United States—a gruelling season she summed up simply: she is not easily broken. Released to celebrate nine years of marriage and serve as the lead single from their forthcoming 2027 album Not Easily Broken, “On My Way” turns that survival story into a joyful Afro-gospel and R&B thanksgiving record. Watching the two of them sing and dance together on screen hits differently once you know what they walked through this year—it is warm, unguarded, and the kind of visual that lifts your whole mood on a quiet Sunday morning. Kakua – Angélique Kidjo feat. Diamond Platnumz Five-time Grammy winner Angélique Kidjo teams up with Tanzanian Bongo Flava giant Diamond Platnumz on “Kakua”, a vibrant cross-continental collaboration linking West and East Africa. Driven by brisk percussion, bright brass accents, and call-and-response hooks sung across French, Yoruba, and Swahili, the track carries an immediate, celebratory pulse from its opening bars. The accompanying visuals match the song’s global spirit with vivid colour palettes, kinetic dance sequences, and celebratory styling that turns every frame into a pan-African street party. Inferno – Peruzzi, Zlatan and Shoday You have probably been listening to “Inferno” non-stop already, jamming to it on playlists, in traffic, and everywhere speakers are turned up—and now the official video takes that same madness to another level. item.title: Damilola Bolarinde Just Made History as Nigeria’s First Miss International Africa
item.description: Damilola Bolarinde styled in a yellow floral brocade cape gown and crown as Miss International Nigeria 2026. Photo Credit: Damilola Bolarinde/Instagram Did you know that since the Miss International organisation introduced continental crowns in 2015, no Nigerian delegate had ever won the regional title—until now? Damilola Bolarinde has officially broken that record, making history as the first Nigerian ever to be crowned Miss International Africa 2026 following the 64th edition of the pageant in Tokyo, Japan. Competing against 73 delegates at Kanadevia Hall (formerly Tokyo Dome City Hall) on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, the Nigerian beauty queen—widely known as Queen Dammy —secured a place in the Top 20 before being named Miss International Africa 2026 on Thursday, 26 November. Beyond bringing home Nigeria’s first-ever continental sash, her Top 20 placement also matched the country’s highest-ever finish in the competition since Nigeria first debuted at Miss International in 1990. Damilola Bolarinde in her Nigerian heritage-inspired national costume for the 64th Miss International pageant. Photo Credit: Damilola Bolarinde/Instagram If you have been following Nigerian pageantry over the past few years, Damilola’s latest milestone will come as no surprise. Outside of pageantry, she works as a model, actress, and entrepreneur, and is the founder of The Unconventional Quest , an advocacy platform focused on helping young Nigerians—particularly women—explore career paths beyond conventional expectations. Her journey to Tokyo was built on years of steady competition on major national and international stages. She earned her spot to represent Nigeria on 19 April 2026 after winning the Face of Hope pageant at the Eko Convention Centre in Lagos, which carried the Miss International Nigeria 2026 title. Before that, she represented Lagos State at Miss Universe Nigeria 2025 , finishing as first runner-up, and won Miss Grand Nigeria 2022 , where she also placed in the Top 20 at Miss Grand International in Indonesia. Damilola Bolarinde during a courtesy visit to Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu after winning Miss International Nigeria 2026. Photo Credit: Damilola Bolarinde/Instagram Reacting to her historic win on Instagram, Damilola reflected on the people and experiences behind the achievement: To everyone who contributed to making this journey possible, please know that I do not take your kindness, sacrifices, generosity, or love for granted. Behind this sash is a young woman who has been carried by the love and support of so many people. To my country, Nigeria, thank you for giving me a reason to dream bigger. To Africa, thank you for the privilege of representing our beauty, strength, culture, and resilience. This is not just a sash to me. It represents every hand that helped me get here, every prayer that covered me, every sacrifice that went unseen, and every person who reminded me that I was never walking this journey alone. item.title: Dropping missiles from orbit? 2 European companies sign agreement to study the idea
item.description:
Julian Dossett is a freelance writer living in Santa Fe, New Mexico. He primarily covers the rocket industry and space exploration and, in addition to science writing, contributes travel stories to New Mexico Magazine. In 2022 and 2024, his travel writing earned IRMA Awards. Previously, he worked as a staff writer at CNET. He graduated from Texas State University in San Marcos in 2011 with a B.A. in philosophy. He owns a large collection of sci-fi pulp magazines from the 1960s.

A pair of companies in Europe have signed an agreement to study the feasibility of developing weapons that can be dropped from orbit. Atmos, a space company known for its Phoenix reusable reentry vehicle , will work with MBDA, Europe's largest missile manufacturer, on the new project. "We are assessing how proven defense systems and new orbital technologies can be combined to strengthen Europe's conventional deterrence and enable future defense capabilities," Sebastian Klaus, the CEO of Atmos Space Cargo, said in a statement on Nov. 18. The system that the companies are investigating is called Precision Orbital Deep Strike, or PODS. The companies said that their initial scope will center on design and feasibility, as well as technology integration. Atmos and MBDA also said this work could lead to demonstrations, but the companies' announcement makes it clear that any deployment or use would be subject to the approval of governmental and military authorities. "The initiative also directly supports MBDA's broader strategic vision in the space domain, reinforcing both space for defense and the defense of space," Thomas Gottschild, MBDA Deutschland managing director, said in the same statement. This news comes a few months after Chief of Space Operations Gen. Douglas Schiess said that the U.S. Space Force operates orbital weapons . "Let me be crystal clear: Today, Guardians operate on-orbit weapons that can defend the joint force against space-enabled attacks," Schiess said during a conferenace presentation on Sept. 15 ("Guardians" refers to Space Force personnel.) Last year, Atmos' Phoenix capsule got its first test run in space. The cargo-return technology launched aboard a Space X Falcon 9 rocket during a rideshare mission in February 2025. Atmos tested out the inflatable heat shields it has been working on to help future space-manufactured cargo make it through Earth's atmosphere in one piece. "Orbital transportation and return form a new layer of strategic infrastructure, and infrastructure determines what Europe can achieve on its own terms," Klaus said in the Nov 18 statement.

item.title: Binance Fully Lifts Withdrawal Suspension a Month After $6.3 Billion Hack
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Binance Fully Lifts Withdrawal Suspension a Month After $6.3 Billion Hack Binance has fully lifted the withdrawal suspension it put in place after last month’s record $6.3 billion hack, saying its recovery work is complete and that withdrawals are open across nearly all networks. “Our withdrawal recovery work is completed and the withdrawal suspension from the security incident has been fully lifted,” the exchange said in an X post Thursday afternoon. A small number of networks remain paused for maintenance, which Binance called standard practice and said was unrelated to the hack. The update closes out a month of phased reopenings. Binance confirmed the breach on Oct. 29, saying its initial investigation pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop that gave the attacker access to a service container, which was then used to submit unauthorized withdrawals. The world’s largest crypto exchange stopped all customer withdrawals for two days after the theft, Reuters reported . When they first reopened, customers pulled a net $4.7 billion off the platform, Binance said on Nov. 2. Binance covered the losses Binance said on Nov. 12 that it had completed coverage of the affected assets with more than $6.34 billion of company funds. The money came from a partial draw on its Secure Asset Fund for Users, part of its futures insurance fund and its corporate treasury, and the exchange pledged to rebuild SAFU to about $1 billion. Coverage is not the same as recovery. Binance replaced the stolen tokens from its own books, while about $2.85 billion of the stolen funds have been frozen remotely by the companies that issue them. The rest remains in the hands of the attackers. U.S. authorities have blamed North Korean hackers for the theft, which North Korea denies. On Nov. 23, the Justice Department moved to forfeit more than $1.1 billion in USDC that Circle froze, and said the U.S. has helped freeze, seize or return more than $2.9 billion since the attack. Launderers turn to THORChain and coinjoin The unfrozen funds are on the move. North Korean launderers have stepped up transfers through THORChain and a coinjoin service in recent days, blockchain researchers told Reuters , as part of an operation spanning tens of thousands of transactions across blockchains. Chainalysis and Elliptic estimate that more than $600 million of the stolen crypto has passed through THORChain, though Elliptic said that figure could count funds that went through more than once. TRM Labs estimates THORChain earned as much as $1 million in fees from the swaps. Separately, $342 million has moved through a coinjoin service mostly coordinated by a pseudonymous figure named Kruw, Elliptic said. A coinjoin combines coins from many users into a single transaction, so their origin is no longer visible on the blockchain. Elliptic has said the launderers will still need other services, such as over-the-counter brokers, to turn the coins into cash. The FBI on Oct. 31 published
